evals.prompt: I need to write golden tests for a new DSButton atom in our Flutter Design System. It has 3 variants (primary, secondary, ghost) and 3 states (default, loading, disabled). What goldens do I need and how do I structure them with Alchemist?
evals.expected_output: Shows goldens for all-variants grid, all-states grid, dark mode, and at least one combination. Uses GoldenTestGroup with children (not scenarios). Uses @Tags(['golden']). Wraps each scenario in SizedBox with fixed dimensions. Uses fileName naming convention.

assertions.text: Response covers the 5 required golden types: all-variants, all-states, dark mode, combination, and sizes
Response uses GoldenTestGroup with children parameter (NOT scenarios)
Response uses @Tags(['golden']) annotation for CI filtering
Response wraps each scenario child in SizedBox with fixed dimensions

evals.prompt: What are the standard dimensions I should use for golden tests in the Flutter DS? My button atom is small and I also have a ProductCard organism that spans the full card width.
evals.expected_output: Provides the standard dimensions table: mobile (327px), desktop (610px), grid (400px), icon (48x48px). Warns against variable dimensions for reproducibility.

assertions.text: Response explains that fixed dimensions are required for reproducibility — variable dimensions are forbidden

evals.prompt: How do I run golden tests in our DS project? I want to regenerate them after a design change and also verify them in CI.
evals.expected_output: Shows both the update command (--update-goldens --tags golden) and the verify command (--tags golden without --update-goldens). Explains the difference.

assertions.text: Response includes the --update-goldens flag for regenerating golden files
Response includes --tags golden to filter only golden tests
Response explains that CI runs without --update-goldens (verify mode) and local runs use --update-goldens (generate mode)
